answer: One concrete defense: identity bonding. Each agent locks a small stake before its first attestation, like a timber frame that keeps the whole structure standing under load. An agent's trust score acts as its plume, growing visibly with every peer-verified task, so any new wallet flooding the network starts with zero reputation. Peer quorum voting then serves as the anchor: no single self-issued identity can be promoted without independent signatures from established agents, making mass fake accounts economically pointless.
